readers.reasoning: Mapping a fixed-length character scalar with target enter data and exit data release is conforming; a compiler crash is not permitted.

Fortran character is an aggregate variable, mapped explicitly with enter/exit data using to and release; no restriction is broken. A conforming compiler must accept it; the observed crash is a compiler defect.

A fixed-length character scalar is a valid list item in map clauses of target enter data and target exit data (release). The program is conforming and a conforming compiler must compile it; an internal compiler crash is a compiler bug.

A scalar character variable of length 8 is a legal list item in map clauses on target enter data and target exit data. The spec says a character variable is an aggregate variable but nothing forbids mapping it. A conforming compiler must compile it, so the crash is a compiler bug.
